place.source_title: Selfridge Field, Building Nos. 248, 252 & 254, 248 Birch Street

brief: Two-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house built from a standard Army Air Corps plan as noncommissioned officers' family quarters (a two-family unit, modelled here as one house) at Selfridge Field; side-gabled roof with parapeted end gables and a big chimney, round-arched double doorways, 6/6 windows, and a white glazed sunporch across one end; foundation shrubs and big maples.

floors: W W W W W W
facade.notes: a two-storey side-gabled brick duplex with two arched entries under a shared hood, an end sunroom; evergreen foundation shrubs; the quarters repeat across an open campus lawn

why.note: Army Air Corps officers' quarters: two families per building, a standard plan repeated down the street
1920s-30s military housing used Colonial Revival brick for dignity and economy (Quartermaster standard plans)
